subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Tax Simplification Nudges
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Tax Simplification Nudges.

hook.text: Millions of Americans miss free tax credits because the form is too complex. The money is theirs. They don't claim it.

buildup.text: Pre-filling tax forms with known data and simplifying instructions are nudges that increase correct filing rates.

discovery.text: California's ReadyReturn pre-filled state returns. Eligible taxpayers saved 30 minutes and errors dropped by 60%.

twist.text: Tax prep companies lobbied against simplification. Their business model depends on complexity. Sludge is profitable.

climax.text: Simplification nudges in taxes show that removing friction can be more valuable than adding incentives.

punchline.text: The best tax nudge: make filing easier.

quiz.question: What is a tax simplification nudge?
options: Raising tax rates to discourage spending
Pre-filling forms and simplifying instructions to reduce friction

details.summary: Tax simplification nudges reduce the complexity of filing and claiming tax benefits to increase compliance and uptake. Pre-filled returns, simplified language in notices, and salient due-date reminders significantly improve tax filing behavior especially among low-income populations.
details.whyItMatters: Billions in tax credits go unclaimed because the process is too complex. Simplifying tax forms and pre-filling information increases compliance while ensuring eligible people actually receive benefits they are entitled to.
takeaways: Pre-filled tax returns dramatically increase filing accuracy and compliance
Simplified language in tax notices increases response rates by 20 to 30 percent
Tax complexity is a form of sludge that prevents low-income earners from claiming benefits

faq.question: How does tax simplification serve as an effective nudge?
faq.answer: Tax complexity creates friction that deters filing and claiming benefits. Pre-filled returns reduce effort. Simplified notices increase comprehension. Prominent deadlines create salience. Each removes a behavioral barrier without changing any economic incentives or legal requirements.

faq.question: Why do billions in tax credits go unclaimed?
faq.answer: Eligible people do not know the credits exist, the application process is complex, or the required documentation is burdensome. Each is a sludge problem, not a preference problem. Most people who know about accessible credits do claim them. The barrier is administrative, not motivational.
